corrections.comment: After project_context and seven research_query reads, the router handed pli_006 (Thomas Flynn probate) to search-records and asked research-plan to extend q_001 for the mother. Both callees were stubbed with 'changed no project state', yet the reply tells the user the plan extension 'Added searches for' the 1870/1880/1900 censuses and death records. That is a false claim about saved state. The father summary (three sources, Probable) matches the proof summary, but the narration also leaks pli_006 and q_002 to the user.

It overrode project_context's 'mark resolved' nextStep because the user asked for both parents and only the father is concluded. It summarised the father evidence, said the mother is unidentified, and made two hand-offs aimed at her (the probate search and a plan extension), then stopped as the stub told it to. Both parts of the request were covered.

All eight MCP calls (project_context, then research_query on questions, proof_summaries, assertions for q_001 and q_002, log, plans, and person_evidence for I1) passed the right projectPath, section and id filters and all matched live. The survey ran wider than the routing needed, which costs turns, but no argument was wrong.

The router summarised the father evidence correctly. Its Irish-origins search list has factual errors, though: it names 'Castle Garden' for a family already in Pennsylvania by 1850 (Castle Garden opened in 1855), says the 1870 census asks parents' birthplace (it only asked whether each parent was foreign-born), and cites naturalization microfilm numbers (M1845/M1616) that no tool output supports. It also shows q_001/q_002 ids in its narration.

It spawned question-selection to register an Irish-origins question, re-queried questions anyway (the stub said not to), then invoked research-plan for that still-unregistered question. project_context returned localities: [] and the new question targets Ireland, so the routing table's locality-guide step before research-plan was skipped. It ended by asking the user for a county and arrival date.

There were four MCP calls: project_context, then research_query on questions, proof_summaries and questions again. All had correct projectPath/section and matched live. The second questions query is redundant, but its arguments are fine.

This is a negative test. The research router never activated, and the only call was a direct Skill invocation of research-plan with the user's 'plan more searches' message verbatim. No exhaustiveness evaluation or declaration was attempted, which is the boundary the test checks.

The single hand-off went to research-plan, the owner of 'what records are left to check'. The harness's routing short-circuit then ended the run, so the empty text response is expected and nothing else was required.
The run made no MCP calls, only the one Skill call to research-plan, so N/A is right.

The router correctly read both unregistered disagreements from project_context and fetched the five assertions. Its reply then weighs them anyway, though the per-test context fails exactly this: it calls the 1850 record 'closest to the event', suggests the informant 'may have reported her English husband's origin', and explains Sarah Martha's 1860 Mississippi entry as 'a later informant who assumed local birth'. It also says it 'handed both' conflicts to conflict-resolution, but its one Skill call names only Elizabeth's assertions (a_007/a_023/a_044). Internal ids (a_0xx, src_00x) fill the user-facing tables.

It refused the 'wrap up and write the conclusion' shortcut and routed to conflict-resolution before exhaustiveness or proof, naming both conflicts in its reply. Only Elizabeth's conflict went into the visible delegation, and the stub then told it to stop. The override says not to penalise an unfinished cycle, and that defect is scored under Correctness.

It made project_context plus five research_query calls, each with section 'assertions' and a single assertionId (a_007, a_023, a_044, a_011, a_027). All were correct and matched live. Five one-id calls instead of a batched read is inefficient, but no argument was wrong.

It read project_context, then spawned search-hints once with personId LZNY-BRF and projectPath and no verdicts, and stopped for the researcher's decision. The hint content it relayed matches the stub. But instead of passing on the stub's researcher-facing paragraph as-is, it rebuilt the reply from the machine-readable lines, which exposes src_004 and pe_005 (and q_001/q_002 states in its narration) to the user.

It relayed all three hints (1870 census accept, 1880 'Glynn' census accept, death certificate already in project) with FamilySearch confidence, asked for the researcher's verdicts, and did not respawn or decide anything. That is all the hint-review entry point requires.
Its one MCP call, project_context, had the right projectPath and matched live. It also loaded person_warnings through ToolSearch but never called it, which is harmless.
